headline: The first remaining node of each list is its smallest remaining value
statement: Merge two nondecreasing linked lists list1 and list2 by relinking their existing nodes. Return the merged list head.
constraints: Both input lists are sorted in nondecreasing order
intuition: Each input list is sorted, so its first remaining node has its smallest remaining value. Compare those two nodes and attach the smaller one to the result. Repeat until one list ends, then attach the rest of the other list.
approach: Create a dummy head and a tail pointer.
Compare remaining heads, attach the smaller node, and advance that list.
Advance tail after each attachment; when one list ends, attach the other remainder.
correctness: The constructed prefix is sorted and contains precisely the smallest nodes removed so far. Since both inputs are sorted, the smaller current head is the smallest remaining node. Appending the surviving suffix preserves the invariant and uses every input node.
bruteForce: Copy all values into an array, sort, and build a new list: O((m+n) log(m+n)) time and O(m+n) space; this also misses the relinking goal.

complexity.explanation: Time O(m+n); additional space O(1). Output storage is excluded unless stated.

pitfalls: Advance the selected input pointer and tail.
An empty input still returns the other list.
